neighbours.label: The stance word that names what a cause, group or tract supports or opposes ('People for ...', 'Mothers Against ...', 'anti-war', 'antitumour'), vs 'for' and 'against' in ordinary physical or benefactive use
fire: She volunteers with Doctors for Peace, a group that campaigns against nuclear weapons.
Thousands joined the anti-nuclear rally outside the parliament building.
He has been a member of Citizens Against Noise since the airport expanded.
The charity Friends for the Earth planted ten thousand trees last year.
Her grandfather wrote A Treatise against Slavery when he was only twenty.
The senator spoke at an anti-poverty conference in the capital.
Students for Fair Trade set up a stall selling coffee in the main hall.
The anti-smoking campaign put warning posters in every bus station.
quiet: She volunteers at the hospital on Fridays and reads to patients in the ward.
Thousands joined the crowd outside the parliament building to watch the parade.
He leaned his bicycle against the fence and walked into the shop.
The farmer planted ten thousand trees for his grandchildren last year.
Her grandfather wrote a long letter to his brother when he was only twenty.
The senator bought a present for her son in the capital.
The students set up a stall selling coffee in the main hall.
The rain beat against the windows of every bus station.
